proofs.proof_tex:
Put \(q=Sd\) and
\[
 A=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\frac{\pi_s^2}{n_s},
 \qquad D_X=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\rho_{sX}(z_{0s})^\lambda.      \tag{1}
\]
We first work in the deterministic experiment
\(\mathfrak E_X(z_0,\Sigma)\).  Fix
\(\xi=(\mathbb Q_\xi;\mu,f,z)\).  Conditional on the donor sample define
\[
 U_{si}=E_{si}-\mu_s-K_N^{-1}\sum_{\ell=1}^{K_N}
 \{Q_{s,t_{s\ell},i}-f_s(X_{s,t_{s\ell}})\}.                   \tag{2}
\]
The donor sample is independent of all unit histories, and the histories are independent across \((s,i)\).  Therefore the variables in (2) are conditionally centered and independent across \((s,i)\).  Boundedness gives \(|U_{si}|\le4B\), so
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_{\mathbb Q_\xi}\!\left(
 \sum_{s=1}^{S}\frac{\pi_s}{n_s}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}U_{si}
 \mathrel{\Big|}(Z_j)_j\right)\le16B^2A.                       \tag{3}
\]

Let \(t_s^0\) be the smallest nearest design index to \(z_{0s}\).  The definition of \(t_{s\ell}\) and two triangle inequalities give
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \|X_{s,t_{s\ell}}-z_s\|_2
 &\le \|X_{s,t_s^0}-\widetilde z_{\ell s}\|_2
       +\|\widetilde z_{\ell s}-z_s\|_2\\
 &\le \rho_{sX}(z_{0s})+\|z_s-z_{0s}\|_2
       +2\|\widetilde z_{\ell s}-z_s\|_2.
\end{aligned}                                                   \tag{4}
\]
Because \(0<\lambda\le1\), powers of order \(\lambda\) are subadditive.  Holder continuity and (4) yield
\[
 |f_s(X_{s,t_{s\ell}})-f_s(z_s)|
 \le C\{\rho_{sX}(z_{0s})^\lambda+
 \|z_s-z_{0s}\|_2^\lambda+
 \|\widetilde z_{\ell s}-z_s\|_2^\lambda\}.                  \tag{5}
\]
Projection onto the cube is nonexpansive, every balanced fold has cardinality at least \(N/3\), and \(\operatorname{tr}(\Sigma)\le qC_\Sigma\).  Consequently
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb Q_\xi}\|\widetilde z_\ell-z\|_2^2
 \le\frac{\operatorname{tr}(\Sigma)}{|I_\ell|}
 \le\frac{3qC_\Sigma}{N}.                                     \tag{6}
\]
The experiment also imposes
\(\|z-z_0\|_2^2\le C_\Sigma/N\).  Expand
\(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{opt}}-\theta_{\mathfrak E}(\xi)\) into the centered sum in (3) and the approximation terms in (5).  Jensen's inequality applied to (6), followed by \((x+y+z)^2\le3(x^2+y^2+z^2)\), gives
\[
 \sup_{\xi\in\mathfrak E_X(z_0,\Sigma)}
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb Q_\xi}
 \{\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{opt}}-\theta_{\mathfrak E}(\xi)\}^2
 \le C\{A+D_X^2+N^{-\lambda}\}.                              \tag{7}
\]
The nearest-site construction is a single measurable function of the observed array and \(X\), selected before \(z_0\) and \(\xi\); hence it is an admissible witness for the first minimax inequality.  When \(\delta_0<1/2\), Lemma \texttt{lem:rough-holder-optimal-recovery-geometry} makes the right side of (7) at most \(CR_{X,\mathrm{opt}}\).

We next prove the deterministic converse.  If two laws \(P_0,P_1\) have targets separated by \(\Delta\) and total variation at most \(1-\eta\), let
\(A_0=\{|\widetilde\theta-\theta_0|<\Delta/2\}\).  On \(A_0\) the error under law one is at least \(\Delta/2\), and on \(A_0^c\) the error under law zero is at least \(\Delta/2\).  Therefore
\[
 \max_{v=0,1}\mathbb E_v(\widetilde\theta-\theta_v)^2
 \ge\frac{\Delta^2}{8}\{P_0(A_0^c)+P_1(A_0)\}
 \ge\frac{\eta\Delta^2}{8}.                                  \tag{8}
\]

For the treated-mean channel, keep responses and donors fixed and, under \(v\in\{-1,1\}\), take independent \(E_{si}\in\{-b,b\}\), where \(0<b<B\), with
\[
 \Pr_v(E_{si}=b)=\frac12+v\varepsilon_s,
 \qquad \varepsilon_s=\frac{\gamma\pi_s}{bn_s\sqrt A}.        \tag{9}
\]
Since \(A\ge\pi_s^2/n_s\), a sufficiently small fixed \(\gamma\) puts every probability in \([1/4,3/4]\).  The target separation is \(4\gamma\sqrt A\).  The Hellinger affinity of the two product event laws equals
\[
 \prod_{s=1}^{S}(1-4\varepsilon_s^2)^{n_s/2}
 \ge\exp(-C\gamma^2/b^2)>0,                                   \tag{10}
\]
because \(\sum_sn_s\varepsilon_s^2=\gamma^2/b^2\).  If \(a_H\) denotes this affinity, Cauchy--Schwarz applied to
\(|p-g|=|\sqrt p-\sqrt g|(\sqrt p+\sqrt g)\) gives
\(\|P_1-P_0\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\le(1-a_H^2)^{1/2}<1\).  Thus (8) gives risk at least \(cA\).  A common admissible donor law for the prescribed \(\Sigma\) is obtained by taking
\(Z=z_0+\Sigma^{1/2}R\), where \(R\) has independent Rademacher coordinates; its standardized fourth moment is \(q^2<B^4\).

For the fixed-design channel set
\[
 q_s(x)=a_0\min_{1\le t\le T}\|x-X_{st}\|_2^\lambda,
\]
with \(a_0>0\) small in terms of \(B,L,d\), and take
\(f_s=q_s/2\), \(g_s=-q_s/2\).  Lemma \texttt{lem:rough-holder-optimal-recovery-geometry} shows that these surfaces are admissible and agree at every design site.  Deterministic zero responses, identical event laws, and identical donors therefore give identical observations, while the targets differ by \(a_0D_X\).  Equation (8) with \(\eta=1\) yields risk at least \(cD_X^2\).

For the donor channel apply Lemma \texttt{lem:full-covariance-location-pair} under strict interior and fourth-moment slack, choosing its nonzero coordinate in a cohort \(s_0\).  Under both laws use
\[
 f_{s_0}(x)=a_1|x_k-z_{0,s_0k}|^\lambda,
 \qquad f_s(x)=0\quad(s\ne s_0),                               \tag{11}
\]
with \(a_1\) small enough for the Holder and boundedness restrictions.  Keep the response and event laws identical.  If \(e\) is the displaced coordinate, the construction in Lemma \texttt{lem:full-covariance-location-pair} and ellipticity give
\[
 |z_{1,e}-z_{0,e}|
 =\frac{c_\eta N^{-1/2}}{\|\Sigma^{-1/2}e\|_2}
 \ge c_\eta c_\Sigma^{1/2}N^{-1/2}.                            \tag{11a}
\]
Thus the donor product laws have total variation at most \(1-\eta\), while (11)--(11a) separate their targets by at least \(cN^{-\lambda/2}\).  Equation (8) yields risk at least \(cN^{-\lambda}\).  Taking the maximum of the three lower bounds and using the two-sided characterization in Lemma \texttt{lem:rough-holder-optimal-recovery-geometry} proves
\[
 \inf_{\widetilde\tau}\sup_{\xi\in\mathfrak E_X(z_0,\Sigma)}
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb Q_\xi}
 \{\widetilde\tau-\theta_{\mathfrak E}(\xi)\}^2
 \ge cR_{X,\mathrm{opt}}.                                     \tag{12}
\]

We now establish the fixed-query bridge.  Fix admissible \(z_0\) and a labelled point
\(\xi=(\mathbb K_\xi;\mu,m,\Sigma)\in
\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\).  Let \(\mathcal X\) be the exact-design sigma-field, \(\mathcal H\) the unit-history sigma-field, and \(\mathcal Z\) the donor sigma-field.  By Definition \texttt{def:fixed-query-kernel-class}, \(\mathcal Z\) is independent of \(\mathcal X\vee\mathcal H\), unit histories are conditionally independent across \((s,i)\) given \(\mathcal X\), and all required centering, support, covariance, and moment conditions hold.  Consequently, for \(\mathbb K_\xi\)-almost every exact design, the conditional observed law with labels is a member of \(\mathfrak E_X(z_0,\Sigma)\) at its central point \(z=z_0\).  Its target is
\[
 \theta_{\mathfrak E}
 =\sum_s\pi_s\{\mu_s-m_s(z_{0s})\}
 =\theta_{\mathrm{ker}}(\xi;z_0).                              \tag{13}
\]
To verify the global support clause in the deterministic experiment, boundedness gives \(|m_s(X_{st})|\le B\) almost surely.  The density lower bound makes this inequality true Lebesgue-almost everywhere, and Holder continuity extends it to every point of \([0,1]^d\); hence \(\|m_s\|_\infty\le B\).  The last equality in (13) uses Definition \texttt{def:fixed-query-functional}; the same positivity-and-continuity argument ensures that each \(m_s(z_{0s})\), and hence (13), is uniquely determined by the observable law.  Applying (7) conditionally proves the nearest-design bound.  If each design contains \(z_{0s}\), then \(D_X=0\), and the exact-site conclusions follow from the geometry lemma.

Suppose instead that \(g_{sT}(z_0)<1\) for every \(s\).  Then the reference pair
\((z_{0s},h_s^\star)\) is feasible in every foldwise anchor search.  Certificate optimality gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 &C_H\|\widehat u_{s\ell}-\widetilde z_{\ell s}\|_2^\lambda
 +C_H\widehat h_{s\ell}^\lambda
 +C_V(Tn_s\widehat h_{s\ell}^d)^{-1/2}\\
 &\quad\le C_H\|z_{0s}-\widetilde z_{\ell s}\|_2^\lambda
 +C_H(h_s^\star)^\lambda
 +C_V\{Tn_s(h_s^\star)^d\}^{-1/2}.
\end{aligned}                                                   \tag{14}
\]
The bandwidth floor makes the final term no larger than a constant times \((h_s^\star)^\lambda\).  Since \(r=0\), every selected fit has nonnegative weights summing to one.  Holder continuity bounds its approximation bias by the first two terms on the left of (14), while conditional independence of whole unit histories bounds its centered variance by \(CA\).  Donor unbiasedness, projection contraction, and (6) at \(z=z_0\), followed by Jensen's inequality and (14), yield
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}
 [\{\widehat\tau-\theta_{\mathrm{ker}}(\xi;z_0)\}^2
 \mid(X_{st})]\le CR_D.                                       \tag{15}
\]
The last assertion of the geometry lemma gives
\(R_{X,\mathrm{opt}}\le CR_D\).

Finally fix \(P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\).  Every defining equality or factorization in the panel class holds outside a marginally null query set; the conditional density and conditional mixing assumptions explicitly hold there as well.  Finiteness of cohorts and dates and countability of mixing lags allow intersection of these conull sets.  Hence, for almost every admissible query, the labelled regular conditional point
\(\xi_{z_0}=(\mathbb K_{z_0};\mu(z_0),m,\Sigma(z_0))\) belongs to
\(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\).  Lemma \texttt{lem:causal-identification} gives
\(\theta_{\mathrm{ker}}(\xi_{z_0};z_0)=\tau(z_0)\) on the same set.  Equations (13)--(15) therefore transfer to the causal conditional kernel for almost every query and almost every exact design.  No decision rule uses the nuisance labels or potential outcomes, and no regular conditional version is selected at a query-null value.

Write
\[
 A=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\frac{\pi_s^2}{n_s},
 \qquad D_T=\left\{\frac{\log(T\vee2)}T\right\}^{2\lambda/d}. \tag{1}
\]
Fix \(z_0\in\mathcal Z_{\delta_0}\) and
\(\xi\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\).  Let
\(\mathcal G=\{g_{sT}(z_0)<1\text{ for every }s\}\).  On \(\mathcal G\), Theorem \texttt{thm:conditional-frontier} gives the conditional risk bound \(CR_D\).  Both \(\widehat\tau\) and \(\theta_{\mathrm{ker}}\) lie in \([-2B,2B]\), so squared error is at most \(16B^2\) on \(\mathcal G^c\).  Since \(0<h_s^\star\le1\),
\[
 \Pr(\mathcal G^c)
 \le\sum_s\Pr(h_s^\star=1)
 \le\sum_s\mathbb E(h_s^\star)^{2\lambda}.                    \tag{2}
\]
The bandwidth floor also gives
\[
 \{Tn_s(h_s^\star)^d\}^{-1/2}\le(h_s^\star)^\lambda.          \tag{3}
\]
Apply Lemma \texttt{lem:geometric-mixing-anchor-moment} to (2)--(3), and use Cauchy--Schwarz followed by Minkowski for the weighted sum of \((h_s^\star)^\lambda\).  Uniformly over the fixed query and labelled point,
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}
 [\{\widehat\tau-\theta_{\mathrm{ker}}(\xi;z_0)\}^2]
 \le C\bigg[&A+
 \left\{\sum_s\pi_s(Tn_s)^{-\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}\right\}^2\\
 &+D_T+N^{-\lambda}\bigg]
 \le CR_\star.
\end{aligned}                                                   \tag{4}
\]
This argument charges every case \(h_s^\star=1\), including an available endpoint anchor and every fallback, and does not use an undeclared response-mixing property.  The rule \(\widehat\tau\) is a function only of the common observable sigma-field and is selected before \(z_0\) and \(\xi\).

The smoothing display is redundant.  With \(a_s=n_s^{-1/2}\) and \(b=T^{-\lambda/d}\),
\[
 (Tn_s)^{-\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}
 =a_s^{2\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}b^{d/(2\lambda+d)}
 \le a_s\vee b.                                                 \tag{5}
\]
Because \(S\) is fixed, Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\[
 \left\{\sum_s\pi_s(Tn_s)^{-\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}\right\}^2
 \le2S\sum_s\frac{\pi_s^2}{n_s}+2T^{-2\lambda/d}
 \le C(A+D_T).                                                   \tag{6}
\]

For the converse, suppose two laws \(P_0,P_1\) have target separation \(\Delta\) and total variation at most \(1-\eta\).  For
\(A_0=\{|\widetilde\tau-\theta_0|<\Delta/2\}\), one of the two squared errors is at least \(\Delta^2/4\) on \(A_0\) or its complement, and
\(P_0(A_0^c)+P_1(A_0)\ge\eta\).  Hence
\[
 \max_{v=0,1}\mathbb E_v(\widetilde\tau-\theta_v)^2
 \ge\eta\Delta^2/8.                                           \tag{7a}
\]
Under \(\delta_0<1/2\) and \(B^4>(Sd)^2\), embed a treated-mean pair at \(z_0=\tfrac12\mathbf1\) as follows.  Choose \(0<b<c\) with \(c+b<B\), use independent uniform exact designs, set every untreated regression and deterministic training response equal to \(c\), and use a common admissible donor law.  Under \(v\in\{-1,1\}\), let the observed treated wealth take values \(c-b,c+b\) independently across units, with
\[
 \Pr_v(B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}=c+b)=\frac12+v\varepsilon_s,
 \qquad \varepsilon_s=\frac{\gamma\pi_s}{bn_s\sqrt A}.
\]
Small fixed \(\gamma\) makes these probabilities admissible.  The target separation is \(4\gamma\sqrt A\), while the product Hellinger affinity \(a_H\) is bounded away from zero because
\(\sum_sn_s\varepsilon_s^2=\gamma^2/b^2\).  Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\(\|P_1-P_0\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\le(1-a_H^2)^{1/2}<1\).  Set treated potential wealth equal to the observed coordinate and untreated event wealth equal to \(c\).  Baseline wealth one, horizon-zero return equal to wealth minus one, and later returns zero verify Definition \texttt{def:buyhold-level}.  Thus both labelled points belong to the same fixed-query class, and (7a) yields the lower term \(cA\).  The two laws of Lemma \texttt{lem:donor-location-two-point-family} have degenerate admissible queries, so their labelled regular conditional points belong to the corresponding fixed-query classes.  Since one rule is chosen before the supremum over query values, that lemma and (7a) yield \(cN^{-\lambda}\).  Lemma \texttt{lem:geometric-mixing-cluster-two-point-family} supplies two labelled points in one fixed-query class with common mass bounded away from zero and target separation of order \(D_T^{1/2}\); it yields \(cD_T\).  Combining the three subexperiments and (6) proves
\[
 \inf_{\widetilde\tau}\sup_{z_0\in\mathcal Z_{\delta_0}}
 \sup_{\xi\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)}
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}
 [\{\widetilde\tau-\theta_{\mathrm{ker}}(\xi;z_0)\}^2]
 \asymp A\vee D_T\vee N^{-\lambda}\asymp R_\star.            \tag{7}
\]

On the independent-calendar subclass, the last part of the anchor lemma replaces \(D_T\) in (4) by \(T^{-2\lambda/d}\).  For the reverse inequality, use i.i.d. uniform design and a cube of radius \(r_T=cT^{-1/d}\) around \(z_{01}\).  Define the smooth product bump
\(\phi(u)=\prod_{k=1}^{d}\psi(u_k)\), where
\(\psi(v)=\exp\{1-(1-v^2)^{-1}\}\) for \(|v|<1\) and zero otherwise.  Take one surface constant and the other equal to that constant plus \(ar_T^\lambda\phi((x-z_{01})/r_T)\), with \(a\) small enough for the Holder and support bounds.  They agree outside the cube and differ at its center by \(ar_T^\lambda\).  For a dimensional volume constant \(v_d\), the hit probability at one date is at most \(v_dr_T^d\), so sufficiently small fixed \(c\) gives
\[
 \Pr\{X_{1t}\text{ misses the cube for every }t\}
 \ge(1-v_dr_T^d)^T\ge c_2>0.                                  \tag{8}
\]
On this event the two observed laws coincide, while their targets differ by \(c_1T^{-\lambda/d}\).  The two-point inequality yields the lower squared-risk term \(cT^{-2\lambda/d}\).

For \(S=1\), \(H=0\), \(p=d=1\), and \(n_1=n\), the unreduced bookkeeping form of (4) is
\[
 n^{-1}\vee(Tn)^{-2\lambda/(2\lambda+1)}
 \vee T^{-2\lambda}\vee N^{-\lambda}.
\]
Equation (6) shows that the smoothing term is dominated by the maximum of the first and third terms.  Finally, every panel law has a labelled fixed-query regular conditional point for marginal-almost-every admissible query, and Lemma \texttt{lem:causal-identification} identifies its observed-law functional with \(\tau(z_0)\).  Applying (4) on that conull set proves the asserted causal transfer without evaluating a null conditional version.

Fix \(z_0\in\mathcal Z_{\delta_0}\) and a labelled point
\(\xi=(\mathbb K_\xi;\mu,m,\Sigma)\in
\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\).  Boundedness gives
\(\theta_{\mathrm{ker}}(\xi;z_0)\in[-2B,2B]\).  On the regular branch \(r=0\).  Conditional on the exact design and donor sample, the selected weights are response-independent, nonnegative, and satisfy \(\sum_tw_{st}=1\).  Define one variable per complete unit history by
\[
 \zeta_{si}=\frac{\pi_s}{n_s}\left[
 B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}-\mu_s
 -\sum_{t=1}^{T}w_{st}\{Q_{sti}-m_s(X_{st})\}\right].           \tag{1}
\]
Donor--panel independence means that further conditioning on donors does not change the conditional unit-history law given the design.  The two centering clauses in Definition \texttt{def:fixed-query-kernel-class} center (1), and its cross-unit condition makes these variables independent across \((s,i)\).  Their range lengths are at most
\[
 d_{si}=\frac{2B\pi_s}{n_s}
 \left(1+\sum_{t=1}^{T}|w_{st}|\right).                         \tag{2}
\]
For a variable \(V\in[a,b]\), convexity of the exponential gives
\(\mathbb E\exp\{u(V-\mathbb EV)\}\le
\exp\{u^2(b-a)^2/8\}\).  Multiplication over the independent variables, exponential Markov, and optimization in \(u\), followed by the definitions of \(A_w,M_w\), imply
\[
 \Pr\left\{\left|\sum_{s,i}\zeta_{si}\right|>r_{\mathrm{unit}}
 \mathrel{\Big|}\mathcal X,(Z_j)_j\right\}
 \le\alpha_{\mathrm{st}}.                                     \tag{3}
\]
The positive linear term in \(r_{\mathrm{unit}}\) only enlarges this radius.  The argument treats one entire unit history as one bounded variable and uses no calendar-score independence.

Put \(q=Sd\).  Spectral clipping gives
\(\widehat\Sigma\succeq(c_\Sigma/2)I_q\).  Every fold has size at least \(N/3\), so donor unbiasedness and
\(\Sigma\preceq C_\Sigma I_q\) give
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}\left[
 N\|\widehat\Sigma^{-1/2}(\overline Z_\ell-z_0)\|_2^2\right]
 \le\frac{6qC_\Sigma}{c_\Sigma}.                              \tag{4}
\]
This uses only the deterministic lower eigenvalue after clipping; it does not require independence of the sample mean and covariance estimate.  Markov's inequality, a union bound over at most two folds, and the definition of \(q_{\mathrm{don}}\) imply
\[
 \Pr\left\{\max_\ell
 \|\widehat\Sigma^{-1/2}(\overline Z_\ell-z_0)\|_2
 >q_{\mathrm{don}}N^{-1/2}\right\}
 \le\alpha_{\mathrm{don}}.                                    \tag{5}
\]
On the complement, \(\widehat\Sigma\preceq2C_\Sigma I_q\) and projection contraction imply
\(\max_\ell\|\widetilde z_\ell-z_0\|_2\le CN^{-1/2}\).

At a selected local-constant fit, nonnegative unit-mass weights and kernel support give
\[
 \left|\sum_tw_{st}^{(\ell)}m_s(X_{st})
       -m_s(\widetilde z_{\ell s})\right|
 \le C\{\|\widehat u_{s\ell}-\widetilde z_{\ell s}\|_2^\lambda
          +\widehat h_{s\ell}^\lambda\}.                       \tag{6}
\]
Holder continuity from \(\widetilde z_{\ell s}\) to \(z_{0s}\), (5), and the defining domination by \(C_H\) bound the deterministic error by
\(r_{\mathrm{bias}}+r_{\mathrm{don}}\).  Combining (3), (5), and
\(\alpha_{\mathrm{st}}+\alpha_{\mathrm{don}}=\alpha\) proves coverage on the regular branch.  Every declared bad branch returns \([-2B,2B]\), which contains the target.  Intersecting a covering interval with this known range preserves coverage.  Thus the coverage probability is at least \(1-\alpha\) for every non-fallback index and equals one on a fallback branch; in particular it implies the displayed uniform asymptotic coverage.

For expected length, on the regular branch \(\sum_t|w_{st}|=1\).  Therefore, with \(A=\sum_s\pi_s^2/n_s\),
\[
 r_{\mathrm{samp}}=r_{\mathrm{unit}}
 \le C(\alpha,B)A^{1/2},                                       \tag{7}
\]
where \(\max_s\pi_s/n_s\le A^{1/2}\).  Let
\(\mathcal G=\{h_s^\star<1\text{ for every }s\}\).  On \(\mathcal G\), certificate optimality at the feasible reference pair
\((z_{0s},h_s^\star)\), together with the bandwidth floor, gives
\[
 r_{\mathrm{bias}}
 \le C\sum_s\pi_s\left\{(h_s^\star)^\lambda
 +K_N^{-1}\sum_{\ell=1}^{K_N}
 \|\widetilde z_\ell-z_0\|_2^\lambda\right\}.                \tag{8}
\]
Donor unbiasedness, ellipticity, projection contraction, and Jensen yield
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}
 \|\widetilde z_\ell-z_0\|_2^\lambda\le CN^{-\lambda/2}.      \tag{9}
\]
The interval length is always at most \(4B\).  Since \(0<h_s^\star\le1\), a union bound and Markov's inequality give
\[
 \Pr(\mathcal G^c)\le\sum_s\mathbb E(h_s^\star)^{2\lambda}.    \tag{10}
\]
Apply Lemma \texttt{lem:geometric-mixing-anchor-moment} to (8)--(10).  Uniformly over all fixed queries and labelled points,
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}\operatorname{length}(C_\alpha)
 \le C\bigg[&A^{1/2}
 +\sum_s\pi_s(Tn_s)^{-\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}\\
 &+\left\{\frac{\log(T\vee2)}T\right\}^{\lambda/d}
 +N^{-\lambda/2}\bigg]+CR_\star.
\end{aligned}                                                   \tag{11}
\]
All observed coordinates are finite under boundedness, every search is over a compact set or a finite grid with a deterministic fallback, and spectral clipping is total.  Thus the undefined-or-nonfinite branch has probability zero.  The conditions \(N<2\) and \(n_s<2\) disappear eventually along the stated growth arrays.  The final term in (11) charges the full interval on \(\mathcal G^c\): by (10), the anchor second-moment bound, fixed positive cohort weights, and fixed \(S\), that contribution is at most \(CR_\star\).  Since \(R_\star\to0\) along the growth array, \(R_\star\le R_\star^{1/2}\) eventually.  The smoothing domination in Theorem \texttt{thm:marginal-phase-diagram} now gives
\[
 \sup_{z_0\in\mathcal Z_{\delta_0}}
 \sup_{\xi\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)}
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}\operatorname{length}(C_\alpha)
 \le CR_\star^{1/2}.                                           \tag{12}
\]
In the independent-calendar subclass, the anchor lemma replaces the logarithmic term by \(T^{-\lambda/d}\).

For the converse, suppose two observed laws with targets \(\theta_0,\theta_1\) have a common subprobability measure \(\nu\) of mass \(\eta>2\alpha\).  Uniform coverage \(1-\alpha-o(1)\) under both laws gives
\[
 \nu\{\theta_0,\theta_1\in I_\alpha\}
 \ge\eta-2\alpha-o(1).                                        \tag{13}
\]
Every interval on this event has length at least
\(|\theta_1-\theta_0|\).  Hence
\[
 \max_{v=0,1}\mathbb E_v\operatorname{length}(I_\alpha)
 \ge|\theta_1-\theta_0|\{\eta-2\alpha-o(1)\}.                \tag{14}
\]
For any two laws, take the dominating measure \(\vartheta=P_0+P_1\) and define
\(d\nu=\min\{dP_0/d\vartheta,dP_1/d\vartheta\}\,d\vartheta\).  Then
\(\nu\le P_0,P_1\) and its total mass is
\(1-\|P_1-P_0\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\), so every total-variation overlap bound below supplies the common submeasure required in (13).

The treated pair used in the marginal proof can have common mass arbitrarily close to one by reducing its fixed \(\gamma\); it yields \(cA^{1/2}\).  For the donor channel, apply Lemma \texttt{lem:full-covariance-location-pair} with \(\eta\in(2\alpha,1)\).  Use a common independent uniform design and, in the displaced cohort, the common regression
\[
 m(x)=b_0+a_0|x_k-z_k^{(0)}|^\lambda,                            \tag{15}
\]
with constant regressions elsewhere, deterministic responses
\(Q_{sti}=m_s(X_{st})\), a common positive treated wealth, and untreated event wealth \(m_s(z_s^{(v)})\) under alternative \(v\).  Small \(a_0,b_0\) verify support and Holder smoothness.  Because the displacement has one coordinate and
\(N\|\Sigma^{-1/2}(z^{(1)}-z^{(0)})\|_2^2=c_\eta^2\), ellipticity gives coordinate separation at least
\(c_\eta c_\Sigma^{1/2}N^{-1/2}\).  The panel coordinates coincide, the donor laws have common mass at least \(\eta\), and (15) makes the targets differ by at least \(cN^{-\lambda/2}\); thus (14) gives the donor lower bound.

Lemma \texttt{lem:geometric-mixing-cluster-two-point-family} supplies, in one fixed-query class, common mass above \(2\alpha\) and separation
\(c\{\log(T\vee2)/T\}^{\lambda/d}\).  Equation (14), followed by smoothing domination, gives \(cR_\star^{1/2}\).  In the independent-calendar class, choose the no-hit cube in (8) of the marginal proof small enough that its common mass exceeds \(2\alpha\); this gives \(cT^{-\lambda/d}\).  These three pairs prove the uniformly honest expected-length converse for every one observable-data interval selected before \(z_0\) and \(\xi\).

For a panel law, membership of its labelled regular conditional point and the equality
\(\theta_{\mathrm{ker}}=\tau\) hold on the marginal-conull query set established in Theorem \texttt{thm:conditional-frontier} and Lemma \texttt{lem:causal-identification}.  Applying (3)--(12) there proves the causal transfer and makes no assertion at a query-null value.

Put \(q=Sd\) and \(\Delta_B=B^4-q^2>0\).  Choose \(a_D>1\) such that
\[
 1<a_D^2<1+\Delta_B/2.                                          \tag{1}
\]
For \(|u|\) in a sufficiently small fixed neighborhood of zero, define \(V_u\in\{-a_D,0,a_D\}\) by
\[
 p_+(u)=\frac{1+u^2}{2a_D^2}+\frac{u}{2a_D},\quad
 p_-(u)=\frac{1+u^2}{2a_D^2}-\frac{u}{2a_D},\quad
 p_0(u)=1-\frac{1+u^2}{a_D^2}.                                 \tag{2}
\]
The probabilities are positive after shrinking the neighborhood, and direct summation gives
\[
 \mathbb EV_u=u,\qquad \operatorname{Var}(V_u)=1.              \tag{3}
\]
Let \(R_2,\ldots,R_q\) be independent Rademacher variables, independent of \(V_u\), and write
\(V_u^{(q)}=(V_u,R_2,\ldots,R_q)^\top\).  At \(u=0\),
\[
 \mathbb E\|V_0^{(q)}\|_2^4
 =a_D^2+2(q-1)+(q-1)^2=q^2-1+a_D^2<B^4.                         \tag{4}
\]
The centered fourth moment is continuous in \(u\), so the strict bound persists on a smaller fixed neighborhood.

Put \(z^{(0)}=\tfrac12\mathbf1_q\) and
\(z^{(1)}=z^{(0)}+\delta_Ne_1\), where
\(\delta_N=c_*N^{-1/2}\).  Since \(\delta_0<1/2\), both paths satisfy the interior restriction for all sufficiently large \(N\).  Under alternative \(v\in\{0,1\}\), take i.i.d. donors whose first coordinate is
\(1/2+V_{v\delta_N}\) and whose remaining coordinates are \(1/2\) plus the common Rademacher coordinates.  Then
\[
 \mathbb E_vZ_j=z^{(v)},\qquad
 \operatorname{Var}_v(Z_j)=I_q,
 \qquad \mathbb E_v\|Z_j-z^{(v)}\|_2^4\le B^4.                \tag{5}
\]
Since \(c_\Sigma\le1\le C_\Sigma\), this covariance is admissible.

The square roots of the three probabilities in (2) have bounded second derivatives near zero; their affinity is one at zero and has derivative zero there.  Thus the one-donor Hellinger affinity is at least \(1-C_0\delta_N^2\).  For densities \(p,g\), Cauchy--Schwarz applied to
\(|p-g|=|\sqrt p-\sqrt g|(\sqrt p+\sqrt g)\) gives total variation at most the square root of one minus squared affinity.  Product factorization therefore gives
\[
 \|P_1^{Z,N}-P_0^{Z,N}\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
 \le\{1-(1-C_0\delta_N^2)^{2N}\}^{1/2}.                       \tag{6}
\]
Choosing fixed \(c_*>0\) sufficiently small makes (6) at most \(1-\eta_0\) for some fixed \(\eta_0>0\).

Use a common i.i.d. uniform exact training design.  If \(0<\kappa<1\), equivalently \(0<\lambda<1\), set
\[
 m_1(x)=b_0+b_1(x_1-1/2)_+^\kappa;
\]
if \(\kappa=1\), equivalently \(\lambda\ge1\), set
\[
 m_1(x)=b_0+b_1(x_1-1/2).                                      \tag{7}
\]
Set all other surfaces equal to \(b_0\).  In the first case, subadditivity of the \(\kappa\)-power proves the required \(\lambda\)-Holder bound because \(\lambda=\kappa\); in the second case, the affine surface has zero derivatives above order one and belongs to every stated Holder class after scaling.  Sufficiently small positive \(b_0,b_1\), depending only on \(B,L\), enforce the Holder radius and boundedness, and
\[
 |m_1(z^{(1)}_1)-m_1(z^{(0)}_1)|
 =b_1\delta_N^\kappa.                                          \tag{8}
\]
Use identical bounded centered training noise, the same training design, and identical positive constant treated observations under both laws.  Set
\(B_{si}(1)=B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) and set the unobserved untreated event wealth to \(m_s(z_s^{(v)})\).  Taking \(W_{si,-1}=1\),
\(R_{si0}(a)=B_{si}(a)-1>-1\), and \(R_{sih}(a)=0\) for \(h>0\) realizes these wealth levels under Definition \texttt{def:buyhold-level}.

We verify membership.  Conditional on either constant query, the uniform design has density one Lebesgue-almost everywhere and beta-mixing coefficients zero.  Thus the query-conditional density and temporal-mixing assumptions hold.  The constructions verify boundedness, Holder smoothness, consistency, transport, and design-conditional centering.  Unit histories are independent across \((s,i)\), with arbitrary within-history dependence allowed.  The donors are independent of the entire common joint panel, and (5) verifies donor independence, unbiasedness, ellipticity, and the fourth-moment bound.  Therefore both laws lie in
\(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\), and their labelled fixed-query kernels lie in the corresponding classes.

The observed panel factors are identical and (6) controls the only differing observed factor.  Lemma \texttt{lem:causal-identification} and (8) give
\[
 |\tau_1(z^{(1)})-\tau_0(z^{(0)})|
 =\pi_1b_1c_*^\kappa N^{-\kappa/2}.                             \tag{9}
\]
This proves the asserted two-law certificate without a class-wide lower local-modulus assumption.

Put \(q=Sd\).  Since \(B^4\ge q^2\), the common donor law
\(Z_j=z_0+U_j\), with independent Rademacher coordinates in \(U_j\), has mean \(z_0\), covariance \(I_q\), and
\(\mathbb E\|U_j\|_2^4=q^2\).  Take it independent of the entire joint panel.

Choose \(\gamma>0\) so small that \(e^{-\gamma}>2\alpha\), and define
\[
 L_T=\left\lfloor
 \frac{\log T-2\log\log(T\vee3)}{|\log\rho_0|}
 \right\rfloor\vee1,
 \qquad p_T=\frac{\gamma L_T}{T}.                              \tag{1}
\]
For all sufficiently large \(T\),
\[
 2p_T\le\beta_0\rho_0^{L_T-1}.                                \tag{2}
\]
Partition the first cohort's calendar into complete consecutive blocks of length \(L_T\).  Independently label each complete block by
\(C_b\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(p_T)\).  Let \(A_T\) be a cube centered at \(z_{01}=\tfrac12\mathbf1_d\) with volume \(p_T\).  Conditional on \(C_b=1\), draw every design point in the block independently uniformly on \(A_T\); conditional on \(C_b=0\), draw them independently uniformly on \(A_T^c\).  At every date in a complete block the marginal density is
\[
 p_T\frac{\mathbf1_{A_T}(x)}{p_T}
 +(1-p_T)\frac{\mathbf1_{A_T^c}(x)}{1-p_T}=1                   \tag{3}
\]
Lebesgue-almost everywhere.  Draw the incomplete block and all other cohorts independently and uniformly.  Thus the fixed-query density bounds hold uniformly.

For a lag \(k<L_T\), past and future sigma-fields separated by \(k\) dates share at most one Bernoulli block label.  Couple one copy by replacing that shared label with an independent copy.  The mismatch probability is
\(2p_T(1-p_T)\le2p_T\); by the coupling inequality this bounds the relevant absolute-regularity distance.  If \(k\ge L_T\), the two sigma-fields use disjoint independent labels and have absolute-regularity coefficient zero.  Since \(\rho_0^k\ge\rho_0^{L_T-1}\) for \(k<L_T\), (2) gives
\[
 \beta(k)\le2p_T\le\beta_0\rho_0^{L_T-1}
 \le\beta_0\rho_0^k.                                         \tag{4}
\]

Let \(E_T\) be the event that every complete-block label is zero and that no point in the incomplete block lies in a fixed smaller concentric cube.  The incomplete-block failure probability is at most \(L_Tp_T=o(1)\), whereas
\[
 \Pr(E_T)=(1-p_T)^{\lfloor T/L_T\rfloor}-o(1)
 \longrightarrow e^{-\gamma}>
 \eta_\alpha:=\frac{e^{-\gamma}+2\alpha}{2}>2\alpha.          \tag{5}
\]
Let \(h_T\asymp p_T^{1/d}\) be the side scale of the smaller cube.  An explicit fixed smooth bump is
\[
 \phi(u)=\prod_{k=1}^{d}\psi(u_k),\qquad
 \psi(v)=
 \begin{cases}
  \exp\{1-(1-v^2)^{-1}\},& |v|<1,\\
  0,& |v|\ge1.
 \end{cases}
\]
It is supported on \([-1,1]^d\), satisfies \(\phi(0)=1\), and all its derivatives are bounded.  Rescale the smaller cube by a fixed factor if necessary so that the support below is contained in it.  For sufficiently small fixed \(a,b_0>0\), put
\[
 m_{10}(x)=b_0,\quad
 m_{11}(x)=b_0+ah_T^\lambda\phi((x-z_{01})/h_T),                \tag{6}
\]
and keep all other surfaces equal to \(b_0\).  A derivative of order \(j\le\lfloor\lambda\rfloor\) of the perturbation is bounded by a constant times \(h_T^{\lambda-j}\), and the top-order Holder seminorm is bounded uniformly in \(T\).  Thus a fixed small \(a\) places both surfaces in \(\mathcal H_d(\lambda,L)\); small \(a,b_0\) also enforce bounded wealth.

Under alternative \(v\), set
\(Q_{1ti}=m_{1v}(X_{1t})\), use the common constant surfaces elsewhere, keep positive treated observations identical, impose consistency, and set untreated event wealth equal to \(m_{sv}(z_{0s})\).  Baseline wealth one, horizon-zero return equal to wealth minus one, and later returns zero give the required buy-and-hold levels.  Conditional centering holds by construction; conditional on the design the unit histories are degenerate and hence mutually independent.  Equations (3)--(4) verify the query-conditional design conditions.  The donors factor from the complete joint panel and satisfy all donor bounds.  Hence both laws belong to the frozen panel class, and their labelled kernels belong to the same fixed-query class.

On \(E_T\), no response is evaluated in the support of the bump.  The restrictions of the two observed laws to \(E_T\) coincide, yielding a common subprobability measure of mass at least \(\eta_\alpha\) for all sufficiently large \(T\).  Finally, Lemma \texttt{lem:causal-identification} and (6) yield
\[
 |\tau_1(z_0)-\tau_0(z_0)|
 =\pi_1ah_T^\lambda
 \asymp\left\{\frac{\log(T\vee2)}{T}\right\}^{\lambda/d}.   \tag{7}
\]
This is the required common-submeasure certificate.

For a panel law \(P\), Definition \texttt{def:target} gives, at every query where the relevant regular conditional expectations are defined,
\[
 \tau(z_0)=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\left\{
 \mathbb E_P[B_{si}(1)\mid z_0]-
 \mathbb E_P[B_{si}(0)\mid z_0]\right\}.                       \tag{1}
\]
Assumption \texttt{ass:consistency} is an almost-sure equality.  Disintegration therefore gives
\[
 \mathbb E_P[B_{si}(1)\mid z_0]
 =\mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0]                    \tag{2}
\]
outside a marginally null set of query values.  Assumption \texttt{ass:event-date-transport} gives, outside another marginally null set,
\[
 \mathbb E_P[B_{si}(0)\mid z_0]=m_s(z_{0s}).                    \tag{3}
\]
There are finitely many cohorts.  Intersecting the conull sets for (2)--(3) and substituting into (1) proves the first display for marginal-almost-every \(z_0\).

Now fix an admissible query and a labelled causal kernel
\(\xi=(\mathbb K_\xi;\mu,m,\Sigma)\in
\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\).  Its consistency clause and the definition of its observed label imply
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}B_{si}(1)
 =\mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}=\mu_s,        \tag{4}
\]
while its transport clause implies
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}B_{si}(0)=m_s(z_{0s}).               \tag{5}
\]
Applying Definition \texttt{def:target} to the fixed-query causal extension and substituting (4)--(5) gives
\[
 \tau(z_0)=\sum_s\pi_s\{\mu_s-m_s(z_{0s})\}.
\tag{6}
\]
The right side of (6) is \(\theta_{\mathrm{ker}}(\xi;z_0)\) by Definition \texttt{def:fixed-query-functional}.  Thus the observed-law functional is related to the causal contrast by consistency and transport; it is not made causal by definition.  No density, mixing, donor, rank, positivity, or inversion condition is used in (1)--(6).

Write
\[
 \rho_s=\rho_{sX}(z_{0s}),\qquad
 D_X=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\rho_s^\lambda,
 \qquad A=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\frac{\pi_s^2}{n_s}.                  \tag{1}
\]
Take a feasible triple \((f,g,z)\) in Definition \texttt{def:joint-product-modulus} and put \(q_s=f_s-g_s\).  If \(t_s\) is a nearest design index to \(z_{0s}\), nonnegativity of every term in the response budget gives
\[
 |q_s(X_{st_s})|^2
 \le \sum_{t=1}^{T}|q_s(X_{st})|^2\le n_s^{-1}.                \tag{2}
\]
The difference of two members of \(\mathcal H_d(\lambda,L)\) is \(\lambda\)-Holder with constant at most \(2L\).  Hence
\[
 |q_s(z_{0s})|\le n_s^{-1/2}+2L\rho_s^\lambda.                 \tag{3}
\]
The donor part of the budget and \(\Sigma\preceq C_\Sigma I_{Sd}\) imply
\[
 \|z-z_0\|_2
 \le C_\Sigma^{1/2}\|\Sigma^{-1/2}(z-z_0)\|_2
 \le C_\Sigma^{1/2}N^{-1/2}.                                  \tag{4}
\]
Splitting the functional difference at \(g_s(z_{0s})\), using (3)--(4), Holder continuity, \(\sum_s\pi_s=1\), and
\(\sum_s\pi_sn_s^{-1/2}\le S^{1/2}A^{1/2}\), gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 |\mathcal T(f,z_0)-\mathcal T(g,z)|
 &\le \sum_s\pi_s|q_s(z_{0s})|
      +L\sum_s\pi_s\|z_s-z_{0s}\|_2^\lambda\\
 &\le C\{A^{1/2}+D_X+N^{-\lambda/2}\}.
\end{aligned}                                                   \tag{5}
\]
Taking the supremum proves the upper bound for \(\Omega_X\).  The same argument with one cohort and no donor displacement proves
\[
 \omega_{s,X}(1;z_{0s})
 \le n_s^{-1/2}+2L\rho_s^\lambda.                              \tag{6}
\]

For the fixed-design lower bounds, let
\(\mathcal X_s=\{X_{s1},\ldots,X_{sT}\}\) and define
\[
 q_s(x)=a\,\operatorname{dist}(x,\mathcal X_s)^\lambda,         \tag{7}
\]
where \(a>0\) is small enough in terms of \(B,L,d\).  Distance to a nonempty closed set is one-Lipschitz, and for \(u,v\ge0\), subadditivity of \(x^\lambda\) for \(0<\lambda\le1\) yields
\[
 |u^\lambda-v^\lambda|\le |u-v|^\lambda.                      \tag{8}
\]
Thus \(f_s=q_s/2\) and \(g_s=-q_s/2\) belong to
\(\mathcal F_{\lambda,L,B}\), agree at every design site, and differ at \(z_{0s}\) by \(a\rho_s^\lambda\).  Taking \(z=z_0\) consumes zero testing budget.  Using this construction in one cohort and then simultaneously in all cohorts proves
\[
 \omega_{s,X}(1;z_{0s})\ge a\rho_s^\lambda,
 \qquad \Omega_X(1;z_0,\Sigma)\ge aD_X.                        \tag{9}
\]

Assume next that \(\delta_0<1/2\).  Choose a coordinate direction \(v\) that points from the corresponding coordinate of \(z_0\) toward \(1/2\).  There is a constant
\[
 0<a_0\le\frac12\min\{c_\Sigma^{1/2},1/2-\delta_0\}
\]
such that \(u_N=a_0N^{-1/2}v\) keeps \(z_0+u_N\) in the \(\delta_0\)-trimmed cube and
\[
 N\|\Sigma^{-1/2}u_N\|_2^2
 \le Nc_\Sigma^{-1}\|u_N\|_2^2\le1.                          \tag{10}
\]
In the affected cohort, a sufficiently small multiple of
\(x\mapsto\{v_s^\top(x-z_{0s})\}_+^\lambda\) belongs to
\(\mathcal F_{\lambda,L,B}\).  Use that same surface as both \(f_s\) and \(g_s\), use zero surfaces in the other cohorts, and take \(z=z_0+u_N\).  The response part of the budget is zero, while the functional separation is at least \(cN^{-\lambda/2}\), because the selected cohort weight is positive.  Therefore
\[
 \Omega_X(1;z_0,\Sigma)\ge cN^{-\lambda/2}.                    \tag{11}
\]
Equations (5), (9), and (11), together with
\(R_{X,\mathrm{opt}}=A\vee\Omega_X(1;z_0,\Sigma)^2\), prove
\[
 R_{X,\mathrm{opt}}\asymp A\vee D_X^2\vee N^{-\lambda}        \tag{12}
\]
under strict interior slack.  Without that slack, (5) still proves
\[
 R_{X,\mathrm{opt}}
 \le C\{A\vee D_X^2\vee N^{-\lambda}\}.                       \tag{13}
\]

Finally, suppose \(g_{sT}(z_0)<1\) for every \(s\).  Since \(r=0\), the Gram matrix is scalar.  Its strict positivity at
\((z_{0s},h_s^\star)\), together with the support of \(K\), implies that at least one design point is within \(h_s^\star\) of \(z_{0s}\).  Hence \(\rho_s\le h_s^\star\).  The bandwidth floor gives
\[
 \{Tn_s(h_s^\star)^d\}^{-1/2}\le(h_s^\star)^\lambda,          \tag{14}
\]
because \((h_s^\star)^{2\lambda+d}\ge(Tn_s)^{-1}\).  Substitute \(D_X\le\sum_s\pi_s(h_s^\star)^\lambda\), (14), and the definition of \(R_D\) into (13) to obtain
\[
 R_{X,\mathrm{opt}}\le CR_D.                                   \tag{15}
\]
This proves every asserted regime without invoking a lower local-modulus assumption.

Put \(q=Sd\).  Select a signed coordinate vector \(e\), with its sign pointing toward \(1/2\) in that coordinate, and set
\[
 w=\frac{\Sigma^{-1/2}e}{\|\Sigma^{-1/2}e\|_2}.
\]
Let \(O\) be an orthogonal matrix sending the first standard basis vector to \(w\).  Because \(B^4>q^2\), choose
\(\epsilon\in(0,B^4-q^2)\) and put \(a=(1+\epsilon)^{1/2}>1\).  For \(u\) near zero define a variable \(A_u\in\{-a,0,a\}\) by
\[
 p_+(u)=\frac{1+u^2}{2a^2}+\frac{u}{2a},\qquad
 p_-(u)=\frac{1+u^2}{2a^2}-\frac{u}{2a},\qquad
 p_0(u)=1-\frac{1+u^2}{a^2}.                                   \tag{1}
\]
At \(u=0\) all three probabilities are strictly positive; hence they remain probabilities for \(|u|\le u_0\), for some \(u_0>0\).  Direct summation gives
\[
 \mathbb EA_u=u,\qquad \mathbb EA_u^2=1+u^2,
 \qquad \operatorname{Var}(A_u)=1.                             \tag{2}
\]
Let \(R_2,\ldots,R_q\) be independent Rademacher variables, independent of \(A_u\), and define
\(V_u=O(A_u,R_2,\ldots,R_q)^\top\).  Then
\[
 \mathbb EV_u=uw,\qquad \operatorname{Var}(V_u)=I_q.           \tag{3}
\]
Orthogonal invariance and independence give
\[
 \mathbb E\|V_u-uw\|_2^4
 =\mathbb E(A_u-u)^4+2(q-1)+(q-1)^2.                            \tag{4}
\]
At \(u=0\), the right side of (4) is
\(a^2+2(q-1)+(q-1)^2=q^2+\epsilon<B^4\).  It is continuous in \(u\), so, after reducing \(u_0\), it is at most \(B^4\) for \(|u|\le u_0\).

Let \(G_u\) be the law of
\[
 Z_u=z_0+\Sigma^{1/2}V_u.
\]
Equations (3)--(4) imply
\[
 z(u):=\mathbb EZ_u
 =z_0+u\Sigma^{1/2}w
 =z_0+\frac{u}{\|\Sigma^{-1/2}e\|_2}e,
 \quad \operatorname{Var}(Z_u)=\Sigma,                          \tag{5}
\]
and
\[
 \mathbb E\|\Sigma^{-1/2}(Z_u-z(u))\|_2^4\le B^4.             \tag{6}
\]

The Hellinger affinity between \(G_0\) and \(G_u\) equals
\[
 a_H(u)=\sum_{r\in\{-,0,+\}}\{p_r(0)p_r(u)\}^{1/2},           \tag{7}
\]
because all other finite-support coordinates have the same law.  The probabilities in (1) stay bounded away from zero near zero, so \(a_H\) has bounded second derivative there.  Also
\(a_H(0)=1\) and
\(a_H'(0)=\tfrac12\sum_rp_r'(0)=0\).  Taylor's theorem therefore yields
\[
 a_H(u)\ge1-Cu^2.                                                \tag{8}
\]
For \(CNu^2\le1/2\), product factorization and
\(1-x\ge e^{-2x}\) for \(0\le x\le1/2\) give
\[
 a_H(u)^N\ge(1-Cu^2)^N\ge e^{-2CNu^2}.                         \tag{9}
\]
For dominated probability laws with densities \(p,g\), Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \|P-G\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
 &=\frac12\int|\sqrt p-\sqrt g|(\sqrt p+\sqrt g)\\
 &\le\left\{1-\left(\int\sqrt{pg}\right)^2\right\}^{1/2}.
\end{aligned}                                                   \tag{10}
\]
Choose \(c_\eta>0\) small enough that (9)--(10), with
\(u=c_\eta N^{-1/2}\), give total variation at most \(1-\eta\), and also choose \(c_\eta\le u_0\wedge1\).  Equation (5) then gives
\[
 N\|\Sigma^{-1/2}\{z(c_\eta N^{-1/2})-z_0\}\|_2^2=c_\eta^2. \tag{11}
\]
Since the coordinate displacement points toward \(1/2\), \(\delta_0<1/2\), and its Euclidean magnitude tends to zero, \(z(c_\eta N^{-1/2})\) obeys the same interior restriction for all sufficiently large \(N\).  Take \(G_0=G_{u=0}\), \(G_1=G_{u=c_\eta N^{-1/2}}\), and enlarge \(N_\eta\) to enforce all preceding restrictions.  Equations (5)--(11) prove the result for the prescribed full covariance.

proposed.def: \(\mathcal M^{\mathrm{iid}}_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\) is the subclass of labelled points in \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\) whose design dates are independent under the kernel component \(\mathbb K_\xi\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: Changing the fixed-query class to labelled points requires the independent-calendar subclass symbol to have the same carrier.

proposed.name: \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\)
proposed.construction:
Fix a deterministic query
\(z_0=(z_{01}^{\top},\ldots,z_{0S}^{\top})^{\top}\in([0,1]^d)^S\), and let
\[
 \mathcal O=\sigma\bigl((X_{st})_{s,t},(Q_{sti})_{s,t,i},
 (B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}})_{s,i},(Z_j)_{j=1}^{N}\bigr)
\]
be the common observable sigma-field.  Define
\(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\) to be the class of labelled parameter points
\[
 \xi=(\mathbb K_\xi;\mu,m,\Sigma),
 \qquad \mu=(\mu_1,\ldots,\mu_S),
 \qquad m=(m_1,\ldots,m_S),                                    \tag{1}
\]
where \(\mathbb K_\xi\) is a causal-data kernel at the fixed query whose observable restriction is a probability law on \(\mathcal O\), and
\[
 \mu_s=\mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}]
 \quad\text{for every }i.                                      \tag{2}
\]
The following pointwise clauses are imposed.  First, for every \(s,i\),
\[
 \operatorname{dist}(z_{0s},\partial[0,1]^d)\ge\delta_0,
 \qquad B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}=B_{si}(1)\ \mathbb K_\xi\text{-almost surely},
 \qquad \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}B_{si}(0)=m_s(z_{0s}),       \tag{3}
\]
\(|Q_{sti}|\vee|B_{si}(0)|\vee|B_{si}(1)|\le B\) almost surely,
\(m_s\in\mathcal H_d(\lambda,L)\), and every \(X_{st}\) is observed exactly.  Second, for every \(s,t\), \(X_{st}\) has a Lebesgue density \(f_{st\mid z_0}\) satisfying
\[
 c_X\le f_{st\mid z_0}(x)\le C_X
 \quad\text{for Lebesgue-almost every }x\in[0,1]^d,             \tag{4}
\]
and the sequence \((X_{st})_{t=1}^{T}\) has beta-mixing coefficients
\(\beta_s(k\mid z_0)\le\beta_0\rho_0^k\) for every \(k\ge1\).  Third, with
\(\mathcal X=\sigma((X_{uv})_{u,v})\), unit histories are conditionally independent across \((s,i)\) given \(\mathcal X\), and
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}[Q_{sti}\mid\mathcal X]=m_s(X_{st}),
 \qquad
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid\mathcal X]=\mu_s. \tag{5}
\]
Fourth, the donors are independent and identically distributed, are independent of the entire joint panel
\(((X_{st})_{s,t},(Q_{sti})_{s,t,i},(B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}})_{s,i})\), and satisfy
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}Z_j=z_0,
 \qquad \Sigma=\operatorname{Var}_{\mathbb K_\xi}(Z_j),
 \qquad c_\Sigma I_{Sd}\preceq\Sigma\preceq C_\Sigma I_{Sd},  \tag{6}
\]
and
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}
 \|\Sigma^{-1/2}(Z_j-z_0)\|_2^4\le B^4.                        \tag{7}
\]
Every estimator and random interval in a minimax, coverage, or expected-length display over this class is required to be \(\mathcal O\)-measurable and to be one rule selected before both \(z_0\) and \(\xi\).  Such a rule may not access potential outcomes or the nuisance labels \((\mu,m,\Sigma)\).  The class consists of labelled fixed-query points; it does not choose a regular conditional version for a panel law at a query-null value.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Each member must be an explicit labelled point on the common observable sigma-field, with the observed treated mean label and a decision rule that is fixed before the query and parameter point.

proposed.name: Fixed-query observed-law functional
proposed.construction:
For a labelled point
\(\xi=(\mathbb K_\xi;\mu,m,\Sigma)\in
\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\), where
\[
 \mu_s=\mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}],
\]
define
\[
 \theta_{\mathrm{ker}}(\xi;z_0)
 =\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\{\mu_s-m_s(z_{0s})\}.                   \tag{1}
\]
This is an observed-law functional on the common observable sigma-field.  Indeed, \(\mu_s\) is the mean of an observed bounded coordinate.  If \(m_s\) and \(m_s^\dagger\) are two Holder-continuous versions of
\(\mathbb E[Q_{sti}\mid X_{st}=x]\) under the same observed law, then they agree almost surely under the law of \(X_{st}\).  The lower density bound \(c_X>0\) implies that they agree Lebesgue-almost everywhere.  Their difference is continuous; if it were nonzero at any point, it would be bounded away from zero on a relative open ball of positive Lebesgue measure, a contradiction.  Thus
 \(m_s=m_s^\dagger\) everywhere on \([0,1]^d\), in particular at \(z_{0s}\), so (1) is uniquely determined by the observed law.  This definition does not identify a causal target.  For a labelled causal kernel, equality with \(\tau(z_0)\) follows from Lemma \texttt{lem:causal-identification} and its consistency and event-date-transport clauses.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The repaired definition makes \(\mu_s\) explicit and proves that density positivity plus Holder continuity turns the conditional-mean equivalence class into a unique point value, while keeping causal identification separate.

proposed.name: Deterministic induced fixed-design product experiment
proposed.construction:
Fix a deterministic array \(X=(X_{st})_{1\le s\le S,1\le t\le T}\), an interior reference path \(z_0\), and \(\Sigma\in\mathbb S_{++}^{Sd}\).  The local deterministic product experiment \(\mathfrak E_X(z_0,\Sigma)\) consists of labelled parameter points \(\xi=(\mathbb Q_\xi;\mu,f,z)\), where \(\mathbb Q_\xi\) is a law of
\[
 \mathcal O_X=\bigl((E_{si})_{s,i},(Q_{sti})_{s,t,i},(Z_j)_{j=1}^{N}\bigr)
\]
labelled by \((\mu,f,z)\), where \(\mu=(\mu_1,\ldots,\mu_S)\in[-B,B]^S\), every \(f_s\in\mathcal H_d(\lambda,L)\) satisfies \(\|f_s\|_\infty\le B\), and
\[
 z\in([0,1]^d)^S,\qquad
 \operatorname{dist}(z_s,\partial[0,1]^d)\ge\delta_0,
 \qquad N\|\Sigma^{-1/2}(z-z_0)\|_2^2\le1.                    \tag{1}
\]
Under \(\mathbb Q_\xi\), \(|E_{si}|\vee|Q_{sti}|\le B\),
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb Q_\xi}E_{si}=\mu_s,
 \qquad \mathbb E_{\mathbb Q_\xi}Q_{sti}=f_s(X_{st}),         \tag{2}
\]
the histories \(((E_{si},(Q_{sti})_{t=1}^{T}))_{s,i}\) are independent across \((s,i)\), with arbitrary dependence within a history, and the donor sample is independent of these histories and is independent and identically distributed with
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb Q_\xi}Z_j=z,\qquad
 \operatorname{Var}_{\mathbb Q_\xi}(Z_j)=\Sigma,\qquad
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb Q_\xi}\|\Sigma^{-1/2}(Z_j-z)\|_2^4\le B^4. \tag{3}
\]
The statistical target is
\[
 \theta_{\mathfrak E}(\xi)
 =\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\{\mu_s-f_s(z_s)\}.                       \tag{4}
\]
Every estimator and interval in this experiment is measurable with respect to \(\sigma(\mathcal O_X)\) and is one rule selected before \(z_0\) and \(\xi\); it may depend on the displayed fixed array \(X\), but not on \((\mu,f,z,\Sigma)\), potential outcomes, or any nuisance label.  This is a deterministic experiment for every \(X\); it does not select a regular conditional distribution at a null design.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The deterministic minimax experiment needs the same explicit rule-before-query convention; its feasible nearest-site witness already satisfies it.

proposed.name: Fixed-query independent-calendar subclass
proposed.construction:
For each fixed admissible query \(z_0\), define
\[
 \mathcal M^{\mathrm{iid}}_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)
 =\left\{\xi=(\mathbb K_\xi;\mu,m,\Sigma)
 \in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0):
 (X_{s1},\ldots,X_{sT})\text{ are independent under }\mathbb K_\xi
 \text{ for every }s\right\}.
\]
Only the design dates are required to be independent.  Responses may remain arbitrarily dependent across dates within a unit history.  The observable-measurability and rule-before-query convention is inherited from \texttt{def:fixed-query-kernel-class}.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The subclass must range over labelled points and state independence under their kernel component, rather than treating a probability law as an element of the repaired labelled class.

proposed.name: Fixed-query product-experiment ordered-modulus handle
proposed.construction:
At a fixed admissible query \(z_0\), solve the ordered-modulus problem for the product of the treated-mean, bounded replicated-regression, realized-design, and full-covariance donor-location experiments indexed by labelled points
\(\xi=(\mathbb K_\xi;\mu,m,\Sigma)\in
\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\), using \(\omega_P\) for the covariance-standardized donor coordinate.  Invert the resulting least-favorable tests using either the whole unit history as the stochastic coordinate or a valid deterministic product-experiment test.  The rate certificate \(R_D\) is not itself this exact ordered modulus, and the statistical target becomes the causal target \(\tau(z_0)\) only through consistency and transport.  Every candidate estimator and interval remains one \(\mathcal O\)-measurable rule selected before \(z_0\) and \(\xi\); it may not inspect potential outcomes or nuisance labels.  No calendar-block score, response-block independence, or query-null conditional version is part of this handle.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The open exact-constant handle must inherit the labelled-class and observable-only decision convention after the fixed-query repair.

proposed.statement:
Let \(P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\).  Then, for almost every admissible query \(z_0\) under its marginal query law,
\[
 \tau(z_0)=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\left\{
 \mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0]-m_s(z_{0s})\right\}.
\]
At a fixed admissible query, every labelled causal point \(\xi=(\mathbb K_\xi;\mu,m,\Sigma)\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\) satisfies
\[
 \tau(z_0)=\theta_{\mathrm{ker}}(\xi;z_0)
 =\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\{\mu_s-m_s(z_{0s})\}.
\]
proposed.justification: This isolates the panel-law almost-everywhere equality from the fixed-query labelled-kernel equality and keeps causal identification separate from observed-law uniqueness.
proposed.gap: Neither the observed-law uniqueness argument nor rolling untreated pseudo-events verifies the event-date transport clause.
proposed.consumer: Every statistical frontier first targets the observed-law functional and invokes this lemma only when transferring to a causal panel law or labelled causal kernel.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The narrowed claim requires the fixed-query definitions and the panel class in its dependency and symbol closure.

proposed_core_edits.proposed:
At a fixed admissible query \(z_0\) and a labelled causal point \(\xi=(\mathbb K_\xi;\mu,m,\Sigma)\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\), the causal target is
\[
 \tau(z_0)=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}[B_{si}(1)-B_{si}(0)].
\]
For a joint panel law \(P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\), the corresponding conditional target \(\tau(z_0)\) and its identification are asserted only for almost every query under the marginal query law of \(P\).
proposed_core_edits.reason: The target metadata must quantify over labelled fixed-query points and preserve the marginal-almost-everywhere panel interpretation.

proposed_core_edits.proposed:
At a fixed admissible query \(z_0\), every member of \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\) is a labelled point \(\xi=(\mathbb K_\xi;\mu,m,\Sigma)\) on the common observable sigma-field \(\mathcal O\), and
\[
 \theta_{\mathrm{ker}}(\xi;z_0)
 =\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\{\mu_s-m_s(z_{0s})\},
 \qquad
 \mu_s=\mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}.
\]
The lower design-density bound identifies every conditional regression \(m_s\) Lebesgue-almost everywhere, and Holder continuity uniquely extends that version to \(z_{0s}\); hence \(\theta_{\mathrm{ker}}\) is an observed-law functional.  Consistency and event-date transport, rather than this definition, imply \(\theta_{\mathrm{ker}}=\tau(z_0)\).  Every estimator and interval is one \(\mathcal O\)-measurable rule chosen before \(z_0\) and \(\xi\), with no access to potential outcomes or nuisance labels.  For \(0<\lambda\le1\), the deterministic fixed-design experiment gives the conditional optimal-recovery bound, and the random-design mean-squared-error and honest expected-length frontiers are uniform over the labelled fixed-query class.  The marginal squared-risk scale is \(R_\star=R_{\mathrm{or}}\vee N^{-\lambda}\), with the independent-calendar spacing replacement on \(\mathcal M^{\mathrm{iid}}_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\).  For each joint panel law, the labelled regular conditional point belongs to the fixed-query class and the conclusions transfer only for marginal-almost-every query.  No null conditional version, lower local modulus, calendar-score branch, or headline result for \(\lambda>1\) is used.
proposed_core_edits.reason: The functional metadata must record observed-law uniqueness, the common decision sigma-field, rule-before-query quantification, and the unchanged rough-Holder rates.

prose_updates.tldr: The paper delivers a fixed-query minimax and honest-length frontier for the rough Holder regime \(0<\lambda\le1\), where \(\kappa=\lambda\).  Each point in \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\) is explicitly labelled as \(\xi=(\mathbb K_\xi;\mu,m,\Sigma)\), but every estimator and interval is one \(\mathcal O\)-measurable rule selected before \(z_0\) and \(\xi\), with no access to potential outcomes or nuisance labels.  The treated mean is observed, and design-density positivity plus Holder continuity makes \(m_s(z_{0s})\) unique under the observed law.  Consistency and the untestable event-date transport equality then identify the cohort-weighted buy-and-hold contrast.  The nonredundant rate channels are treated replication, query-conditional calendar spacing, and full-covariance donor location.  Conditional design independence removes the geometric-mixing logarithm; higher smoothness, uniform-in-query bands, and exact phase-intersection constants remain open.

project_justification.gap: Classical fixed-point regression does not combine replicated sites with an external full-covariance generated query, and a panel regular conditional law is only determined marginal-almost-everywhere in that query.  Without an explicit observable sigma-field and labelled-parameter convention, a minimax display can also accidentally admit a query- or nuisance-dependent oracle rule.
project_justification.niche: Historical paths can be observed exactly while only the event-date counterfactual path is synthesized from donors.  A labelled fixed-query class separates the law available to the decision rule from nuisance labels used to index the model, while an almost-everywhere bridge keeps the causal panel interpretation version invariant.
project_justification.fill: The note defines \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\) as labelled points on one observable sigma-field \(\mathcal O\), proves that \(\mu_s\) and \(m_s(z_{0s})\) are observed-law functionals, and restricts every competitor to one observable-data rule chosen before the query and label.  For \(0<\lambda\le1\), nearest-site and anchor/extrapolation estimators attain the conditional and marginal risk rates, while a whole-unit bounded-range interval attains the honest expected-length rate.  Treated, clustered-spacing, and overlapping donor pairs give matching converses, and causal equality is proved separately from consistency and event-date transport.

sampling_model.design: At each fixed admissible query, the statistical model consists of labelled points \(\xi=(\mathbb K_\xi;\mu,m,\Sigma)\) whose observable restriction is on \(\mathcal O=\sigma((X_{st}),(Q_{sti}),(B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}),(Z_j))\).  Each exact pre-event path has a density between \(c_X\) and \(C_X\) Lebesgue-almost-everywhere, and each cohort design sequence is geometrically beta mixing.  The independent-calendar subclass imposes independence only on the design dates.  Every decision rule is chosen before \(z_0\) and \(\xi\).
sampling_model.units: Each cohort supplies \(n_s\) replicated untreated blocks at every date and \(n_s\) treated event observations with common observed mean \(\mu_s\).  Conditional on the exact design, histories are independent across units, while dependence across all dates and the event outcome inside one unit history remains unrestricted.  Sampling concentration treats the complete history as one bounded observation.
sampling_model.treatment: Consistency identifies observed event wealth with treated potential wealth.  Event-date transport separately equates the unobserved untreated event mean with the historical regression at the realized path.  These labelled causal clauses imply equality between the causal target and the observed-law functional; neither density positivity nor design centering proves transport.
sampling_model.overlap: Every admitted fixed query lies at least \(\delta_0\) from the cube boundary.  Density positivity identifies a conditional regression Lebesgue-almost-everywhere, and Holder continuity then uniquely determines its value at the query.  Exact-site recovery can be easier than an anchor certificate; the regular donor converse additionally needs \(\delta_0<1/2\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Only the event query is generated.  Donor folds provide projected means, and the full stacked covariance retains every cross-coordinate, cross-horizon, and cross-cohort covariance.  Nuisance labels index the model but are unavailable to estimators and intervals.  For \(0<\lambda\le1\), nonnegative local-constant weights allow whole-unit concentration without response mixing, deconvolution, calendar-score studentization, or division by an estimated variance.

prose_updates.related_work: Donoho (1994) relates a linear-functional modulus to minimax recovery in a known Gaussian convex experiment; the conditional theorem here instead constructs a bounded treated-response-donor product experiment with an external full-covariance query, a nearest-site characterization, an observable-only decision class, and a separate marginal-almost-everywhere causal bridge.  Akhavan, Gogolashvili, and Tsybakov (2024) study independently estimated minimizers under strong convexity, where center error is second order rather than a rough-Holder donor modulus.  Stone (1982), Fan (1993), Fan et al. (1997), and Gaiffas (2007) provide ordinary Holder, pointwise local-polynomial, kernel-efficiency, and random-design benchmarks; none supplies this labelled fixed-query replicated-panel frontier.  Mammen, Rothe, and Schienle (2012), Delaigle, Hall, and Meister (2008), and Fan and Truong (1993) perturb training coordinates, unlike the exact historical design here; Hahn and Ridder (2013) gives smooth generated-regressor expansions rather than this nonsmooth location modulus.  Armstrong and Kolesar (2018, 2020) provide ordered-modulus and bias-aware ordinary-regression intervals, while Low (1997) motivates fixing the smoothness class.  Cattaneo, Feng, and Titiunik (2021), Kunsch (1989), and Chernozhukov, Wuthrich, and Zhu (2021) concern dependent prediction, resampling, or conformal architectures; the present interval instead concentrates independent whole-unit histories and uses no calendar calibration.  Ferman (2021) motivates many-control replication, while Abadie (2021) and Arkhangelsky and Imbens (2024) frame panel causal assumptions; none validates event-date transport or supplies the fixed-query statistical frontier.
prose_updates.interpretation: The labels \(\mu,m,\Sigma\) specify which member of the fixed-query model generated the data, but they are not inputs to the estimator or interval.  The observable law determines \(\mu_s\) directly and determines \(m_s(z_{0s})\) through density positivity and Holder continuity.  Donor uncertainty dominates when \(N^{-\lambda}\) exceeds treated replication and conditional spacing.  For a causal panel law, the statistical conclusions and the consistency-plus-transport identification step apply only at marginal-almost-every realized query.  Inference requires no calendar response mixing because it conditions on design and donors and concentrates across independent unit histories.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: Every constructive headline is restricted to \(0<\lambda\le1\), fixed admissible queries, and observable-data rules selected before the query and labelled parameter point.  Panel-law statements hold only marginal-almost-everywhere and are not uniform-in-query bands.  For \(\lambda>1\), signed higher-order weights lack the required whole-history stochastic-norm control.  Geometric conditional design mixing retains a logarithmic spacing penalty; only conditional design independence removes it.  The donor converse needs \(B^4>(Sd)^2\) and \(\delta_0<1/2\).  The total interval is rate-optimal but conservative, and exact phase-intersection constants remain open.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The fixed-query class is a labelled statistical model, not an oracle decision problem: every estimator and interval is \(\mathcal O\)-measurable, is selected before \(z_0\) and \(\xi\), and cannot inspect potential outcomes or \(\mu,m,\Sigma\).  Event-date transport remains an untestable causal restriction.  Query-conditional density and design mixing are observed-law restrictions, while design-conditional centering is a separate response restriction.  Donor-panel separation factors donors from the complete joint panel and permits arbitrary temporal dependence within a unit history.  Risk, coverage, and expected length are uniform over labelled points at a fixed query; each panel law inherits them only for marginal-almost-every query.  Higher smoothness, growing dimension, adaptation, uniform-in-query bands, and exact constants are outside scope.

proofs.proof_tex:
Fix \(z_0\) and
\(\xi=(\mathbb K_\xi;\mu,m,\Sigma)\in
\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\).  The bounded-wealth and consistency
clauses of \texttt{def:fixed-query-kernel-class} imply
\(|B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}|\le B\) almost surely, so all expectations below
exist.  The label definition and the design-conditional-centering clause
give
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}
 [B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}-\mu_s\mid\mathcal X]=0.
 \tag{1}
\]
For bounded \(\mathcal X\)-measurable \(W\), the pull-out and tower
properties of conditional expectation yield
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}[(B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}-\mu_s)W]
 &=\mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}\!\left[
 W\,\mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}
 (B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}-\mu_s\mid\mathcal X)\right]\\
 &=0.
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{2}
\]
This proves the asserted orthogonality.

Let \(E\in\mathcal X\) and set \(p_E=\mathbb K_\xi(E)\).  Taking
\(W=\mathbf 1_E\) in (2) gives
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}
 [B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mathbf 1_E]=\mu_sp_E.
 \tag{3}
\]
If \(p_E>0\), division by \(p_E\) gives
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid E]=\mu_s.
 \tag{4}
\]
Applying the same argument to \(E^c\) gives
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid E^c]=\mu_s
 \tag{5}
\]
when \(p_E<1\).  Thus (4)--(5) hold simultaneously when
\(0<p_E<1\), and \texttt{lem:common-design-shock-obstruction} supplies the
stated exclusion.  By \texttt{lem:panel-fixed-query-kernel-transfer}, every
\(P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\) induces a labelled point
\(\xi_P(z_0)\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\) for almost every query.
Applying (1)--(5) to those points proves the panel-to-kernel transfer and
makes no claim at a null-version query.

We now construct the two labelled points.  For arbitrary positive integers
\(N,T,n_1\), take
\[
 S=1,\quad \pi_1=1,\quad H=0,\quad p=d=1,\quad z_0=\frac12,
 \quad \lambda=\kappa=1,\quad B=L=1,\quad \delta_0=\frac14,
 \tag{6}
\]
and set \(c_X=C_X=c_\Sigma=C_\Sigma=1\), with any fixed \(\beta_0>0\)
and \(\rho_0\in(0,1)\).  These values satisfy all declared parameter
ranges, and \(d=p(H+1)=1\).

On a product probability space let \((X_{1t})_{t=1}^{T}\),
\((\eta_j)_{j=1}^{N}\), and \((\varepsilon_i)_{i=1}^{n_1}\) be mutually
independent, with
\[
 X_{1t}\stackrel{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}\operatorname{Unif}[0,1],
 \qquad
 \mathbb P(\eta_j=1)=\mathbb P(\eta_j=-1)=\frac12,
 \qquad
 \mathbb P(\varepsilon_i=1)=\mathbb P(\varepsilon_i=-1)=\frac12.
 \tag{7}
\]
Define
\[
 m_1(x)=\frac12,
 \qquad
 Q_{1ti}=m_1(X_{1t})=\frac12,
 \qquad
 Z_j=\frac12+\eta_j.
 \tag{8}
\]
For every event unit set \(W_{1i,-1}=1/2\) and \(R_{1i0}(0)=0\).
Definition \texttt{def:buyhold-level} then gives
\[
 B_{1i}(0)=\frac12.
 \tag{9}
\]
Under \(\mathbb K_0\), set \(R_{1i0}(1)=0\); under \(\mathbb K_1\), set
\(R_{1i0}(1)=\varepsilon_i/2\).  In each case impose consistency by setting
\(B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}=B_{1i}(1)\).  Hence
\[
 B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}=\frac12\quad\text{under }\mathbb K_0,
 \qquad
 B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}=\frac12+\frac14\varepsilon_i
 \quad\text{under }\mathbb K_1.
 \tag{10}
\]
The smallest constructed return is \(-1/2>-1\), so the return support is
respected.

For \(r\in\{0,1\}\), give \(\mathbb K_r\) the labels
\[
 \mu_1=\frac12,\qquad m_1(x)=\frac12,\qquad \Sigma=1,
 \tag{11}
\]
and call the resulting point \(\xi^{(r)}\).  We verify membership.
Equations (8)--(10) imply
\[
 |Q_{1ti}|=\frac12,
 \qquad |B_{1i}(0)|=\frac12,
 \qquad |B_{1i}(1)|\le\frac34,
 \tag{12}
\]
so bounded wealth holds.  The constant \(m_1\) has supremum norm \(1/2\),
zero derivative, and zero Lipschitz seminorm; hence
\(m_1\in\mathcal H_1(1,1)\).  Moreover,
\[
 \operatorname{dist}\!\left(\frac12,\partial[0,1]\right)
 =\frac12\ge\delta_0,
 \qquad
 f_{1t\mid z_0}(x)=1
 \quad\text{for Lebesgue-almost every }x\in[0,1].
 \tag{13}
\]
The design dates are independent, so
\[
 \beta_1(k\mid z_0)=0\le\beta_0\rho_0^k,
 \qquad k\ge1.

\[

 =\frac12=m_1(X_{1t}),
 \qquad
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_r}[B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid\mathcal X]

 \tag{15}

by \((\eta_j)_j\), while the joint panel is generated by \((X_{1t})_t\)
and, under \(\mathbb K_1\), \((\varepsilon_i)_i\).  Thus (7) also proves

\[

\]
and

 \tag{17}
\]

\]

verify every clause of \texttt{def:fixed-query-kernel-class}.  Therefore
\[

 \tag{19}
\]

satisfies every member property of \texttt{def:panel-model-class}; the

\[

\]
without selecting a null conditional version.

The joint law of \(((X_{1t})_t,(Q_{1ti})_{t,i},(Z_j)_j)\) is common to
\(\mathbb K_0\) and \(\mathbb K_1\) by (7)--(8).  By
\texttt{def:target}, (9)--(10), and \(\mathbb E\varepsilon_i=0\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}

 &=\mathbb E_{\mathbb K_0}[B_{1i}(1)-B_{1i}(0)]=0,\\
 \tau_{\mathbb K_1}(z_0)
 &=\mathbb E_{\mathbb K_1}[B_{1i}(1)-B_{1i}(0)]
 =\frac14\mathbb E\varepsilon_i=0.
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{21}
\]

\(\mathcal X\) give
\[

 \qquad

 \tag{22}

while holding the training experiment, donor experiment, and causal target
fixed.  This is the claimed explicit certificate.

Put
\[

 \qquad

\]

consistency imply \(|B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}|\le B\) almost surely, so the
displayed expectation is finite.  Since \(E\in\mathcal X\), the assumed
equality \(B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}=b\mathbf 1_E\) gives

 \tag{1}
\]

\texttt{def:fixed-query-kernel-class} gives instead

 \end{aligned}

\]

\texttt{def:fixed-query-kernel-class}.

\]

 \tag{3}

\(s,t\), a conditional density satisfying
\[

 \quad\text{for Lebesgue-almost every }x\in[0,1]^d

\]

proposed.name: \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\)
proposed.construction:
Fix a deterministic query
\(z_0=(z_{01}^{\top},\ldots,z_{0S}^{\top})^{\top}\in([0,1]^d)^S\), and let
\[
 \mathcal O=\sigma\!\left((X_{st})_{s,t},(Q_{sti})_{s,t,i},
 (B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}})_{s,i},(Z_j)_{j=1}^{N}\right)
\]
be the common observable sigma-field.  A member of
\(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\) is a labelled parameter point
\[
 \xi=(\mathbb K_\xi;\mu,m,\Sigma),
 \qquad \mu=(\mu_1,\ldots,\mu_S),
 \qquad m=(m_1,\ldots,m_S),
\]
where \(\mathbb K_\xi\) is a probability law for the complete causal-data
array at the fixed query, its observable restriction is a law on
\(\mathcal O\),
\[
 \mu_s=\mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}],
 \qquad
 \Sigma=\operatorname{Var}_{\mathbb K_\xi}(Z_j),
\]
and the following pointwise conditions hold.  First, for every \(s,i\),
\[
 \operatorname{dist}(z_{0s},\partial[0,1]^d)\ge\delta_0,
 \qquad
 B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}=B_{si}(1)\ \text{almost surely},
 \qquad
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}B_{si}(0)=m_s(z_{0s}),
\]
\(|Q_{sti}|\vee|B_{si}(0)|\vee|B_{si}(1)|\le B\) almost surely,
\(m_s\in\mathcal H_d(\lambda,L)\), and every \(X_{st}\) is observed
exactly.  Second, for every \(s,t\), \(X_{st}\) has a Lebesgue density
\(f_{st\mid z_0}\) satisfying
\[
 c_X\le f_{st\mid z_0}(x)\le C_X
 \quad\text{for Lebesgue-almost every }x\in[0,1]^d,
\]
and, for every \(s\), the sequence \((X_{st})_{t=1}^{T}\) has beta-mixing
coefficients
\(\beta_s(k\mid z_0)\le\beta_0\rho_0^k\) for all \(k\ge1\).  Third, with
\(\mathcal X=\sigma((X_{uv})_{u,v})\), unit histories are conditionally
independent across \((s,i)\) given \(\mathcal X\), and
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}[Q_{sti}\mid\mathcal X]=m_s(X_{st}),
 \qquad
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid\mathcal X]=\mu_s.
\]
Fourth, the donors are independent and identically distributed, are
independent of the entire joint panel
\(((X_{st})_{s,t},(Q_{sti})_{s,t,i},(B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}})_{s,i})\), and
satisfy
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}Z_j=z_0,
 \qquad
 c_\Sigma I_{Sd}\preceq\Sigma\preceq C_\Sigma I_{Sd},
 \qquad
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}
 \|\Sigma^{-1/2}(Z_j-z_0)\|_2^4\le B^4.
\]
The statistical experiment reveals only \(\mathcal O\).  Every estimator
and random interval appearing in a minimax or honesty assertion is a single
\(\mathcal O\)-measurable decision rule fixed before \(z_0\) and \(\xi\)
are selected; it may not access the potential outcomes or the nuisance
labels \((\mu,m,\Sigma)\).  This is a class of fixed-query labelled kernels,
not a choice of a regular conditional version at a query-null value.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The fixed-query experiment needs labelled parameter points on one observable sigma-field so decision rules cannot read potential outcomes or nuisance labels and are selected before Nature chooses the query and parameter point.

proposed.name: Fixed-query observed-law functional
proposed.construction:
For a labelled point
\(\xi=(\mathbb K_\xi;\mu,m,\Sigma)\in
\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\), define
\[
 \theta_{\mathrm{ker}}(\xi;z_0)
 =\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\{\mu_s-m_s(z_{0s})\}.
\]
This is uniquely determined by the observable law
\(\mathbb K_\xi\vert_{\mathcal O}\).  Indeed, \(\mu_s\) is the observable
mean of \(B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\).  If \(m_s\) and \(\widetilde m_s\) are
two continuous versions of
\(\mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}[Q_{sti}\mid X_{st}=x]\), uniqueness of
conditional expectation gives
\(m_s(X_{st})=\widetilde m_s(X_{st})\) almost surely.  For every measurable
\(A\subseteq[0,1]^d\), the lower density bound gives
\[
 \mathbb K_\xi(X_{st}\in A)
 =\int_A f_{st\mid z_0}(x)\,dx
 \ge c_X\operatorname{Leb}_d(A).
\]
Consequently the two versions agree Lebesgue-almost everywhere.  Their
difference is continuous, so a nonzero value at any point of \([0,1]^d\)
would persist on a relatively open set of positive Lebesgue measure, a
contradiction.  Thus \(m_s=\widetilde m_s\) everywhere, in particular at
\(z_{0s}\).  The displayed map is therefore an observed-law functional.
It does not define the causal target; equality with \(\tau(z_0)\) follows
from \texttt{lem:causal-identification} at labelled fixed-query points and
at marginal-almost-every query for panel laws.

Statistical decision rules observe only \(\mathcal O\) and cannot access potential outcomes or nuisance labels.

proposed_core_edits.proposed: At a fixed admissible query \(z_0\), a labelled point \(\xi=(\mathbb K_\xi;\mu,m,\Sigma)\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\) has the observed-law functional \(\theta_{\mathrm{ker}}(\xi;z_0)=\sum_s\pi_s\{\mu_s-m_s(z_{0s})\}\), where \(\mu_s=\mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\).  The bound \(f_{st\mid z_0}\ge c_X>0\) identifies every conditional-mean version \(m_s\) Lebesgue-almost everywhere, and Holder continuity uniquely extends it to \(z_{0s}\); hence \(\theta_{\mathrm{ker}}\) is determined by \(\mathbb K_\xi\vert_{\mathcal O}\).  Consistency and event-date transport prove \(\theta_{\mathrm{ker}}(\xi;z_0)=\tau(z_0)\) for labelled causal fixed-query points and prove the panel-law equality only for marginal-almost-every query.  Every minimax estimator and interval is one \(\mathcal O\)-measurable rule chosen before \(z_0\) and \(\xi\), with no access to potential outcomes or \((\mu,m,\Sigma)\).  For \(0<\lambda\le1\), the deterministic fixed-design experiment supplies the conditional optimal-recovery bound, while random-design MSE and honest expected-length bounds and converses are uniform over this labelled fixed-query class; the marginal squared-risk scale is \(R_\star=R_{\mathrm{or}}\vee N^{-\lambda}\), with the independent-calendar spacing replacement on \(\mathcal M^{\mathrm{iid}}_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\).  The feasible interval uses whole-unit concentration and no calendar-score branch.  No supremum is taken over panel-specific values of a regular conditional law at a null query, no lower local modulus is assumed, and no headline result is claimed for \(\lambda>1\).
proposed_core_edits.reason: The metadata must reflect the labelled experiment, observed-law uniqueness, common decision-rule information set, rough-Holder scope, and almost-everywhere causal bridge after the class correction.
